title: Origenes Adamantius: Tractatus super Leviticum
shelf_note: A 12th-century Wolfenbüttel (HAB) manuscript of Rufinus' Latin Origen, Homilies on Leviticus. The pages match the title: hostia pro delicto (hom. 5), leprosy and scars (hom. 8), and 'Explicit liber xi. Incipit xii. De magno sacerdote'. No tradition or collection is given to test it against.
structure_note: There are no structure counts, and none of the three pages carries a translation, so only OCR can be judged. Page 47 has the folio number '22' in modern pencil, and the OCR records it correctly as <page-num>22</page-num>. Pages 92 and 136 are versos with the facing recto visible at the right edge, which is what a normal opening looks like. Nothing suggests a splice or the wrong work.

The scriptural lemma 'Et sacerdos inquid magnus…' is split off with a <margin>"</margin> line and a markdown '>' blockquote in the middle of the sentence 'lex prophetico spiritu scribit. Et sacerdos…'.

book_verdict: The OCR of a difficult 12th-century book hand is faithful almost word for word: abbreviations are expanded correctly and every page is the right leaf. The flaws are layout ones (a rubric spliced mid-sentence on p.136, marginal quotation marks emitted as stray lines) plus one normalised scribal reading ('magnificabo'). There is no translation yet, so a reader gets Latin only.
